locator.section: Article1(1); Article2(2) at physical2 assigns jurisdiction for the Länder

correction: Administrative ownership and nationwide legal standards are distinct. The Länder treaty establishes the ZFU as an NRW institution, makes it the authority for the Länder and gives every state a representative on its administrative committee. A single nationwide authority can therefore operate through joint state administration. If the author means the existing federal statutory framework rather than administrative ownership, describing standards as remaining at federal level can be defensible.
effect: Unresolved. On the literal administrative reading, the claimed federal-to-state institutional transfer is misstated. That correction does not defeat the separate concern that abolishing a joint central review can leave dispersed funding offices making different assessments.
limits: Does not establish that decentralisation is harmless, that the proposed reform is wise, or that federal law has no role. No categorical institutional accusation is promoted. Exact August draft unavailable.
context_and_alternatives: All four author pages read; physical1 visually checked. The paper repeatedly contrasts Bund with16Länder but also acknowledges the Länder treaty and seeks bundesweite/bundeseinheitliche standards. Strongest rescue is federal statutory responsibility for uniform minimum criteria, not a claim that ZFU belongs administratively to the federal government. TreatyArticles1,2,4,14selected; federal vocational-training participation underArticle9 is separate.
materiality_explanation: Potentially minor institutional-description error. The practical preference for one nationwide assessment remains available under the actual Länder arrangement, so a major policy effect is not shown.
